mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and lower corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS dropped by more than 100,000 in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods with sustained PCE growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production by more than 1% in a month indicates supply chain disruptions, which can lead to reduced output and lower corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the unemployment rate rises by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month, it signals a tightening monetary policy coupled with labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and UNRATE rise > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the periods with a sustained decline in the unemployment rate.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts decline by more than 10% in a month and consumer price index (CPI) increases by more than 0.5% in the same month, it indicates a weakening demand coupled with inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 10% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in GDP by more than 1% in a quarter signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the quarters with a GDP increase of more than 1%.
